sources.label: Delaware cyber oversight cases
sources.instrument: Firemen's Retirement System of St. Louis v. Sorenson, C.A. No. 2019-0965-LWW (Del. Ch. 5 Oct. 2021); Construction Industry Laborers Pension Fund v. Bingle, C.A. No. 2021-0940-SG (Del. Ch. 6 Sep. 2022), Final Order and Judgment 13 Oct. 2022, aff'd by order No. 411, 2022 (Del. 17 May 2023); In re The Boeing Co. Derivative Litig., C.A. No. 2019-0907-MTZ (Del. Ch. 7 Sep. 2021); United Food & Commercial Workers Union v. Zuckerberg, 262 A.3d 1034 (Del. 2021); Marchand v. Barnhill, 212 A.3d 805 (Del. 2019); Giuliano v. Grenfell-Gardner, C.A. No. 2021-0452-KSJM (Del. Ch. 2 Sep. 2025); Brewer v. Turner, C.A. No. 2023-1284-KSJM (Del. Ch. 29 Sep. 2025), 2025 WL 2769895, certification denied 2025 WL 3048942 (Del. Ch. 30 Oct. 2025), interlocutory appeal refused sub nom. Turner v. Brewer, No. 444, 2025 (Del. 15 Dec. 2025) (ORDER); In re TransUnion, 324 A.3d 869 (Del. Ch. 2024), C.A. No. 2022-1103-LWW (Del. Ch. 1 Oct. 2024) (Will, V.C.), distinguished in LACERS v. Sanford, C.A. No. 2024-0998-KSJM (Del. Ch. 16 Jan. 2026); Marchner v. Riley, C.A. No. 2025-0164-LWW (Del. Ch. 30 Mar. 2026) (Will, V.C.)
sources.version: dates corrected 2026-08-08; two were wrong before this check. TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS, NEITHER OF WHICH OPENED A SLIP OPINION: the RW-001 dossier's primary-source pass (Chancery PDF headers, the Supreme Court's affirming order quoting its own record) and corroboration from authoritative secondary reporting (Potter Anderson, Morris James), plus the Court of Chancery's published opinion records and CourtListener. This row does NOT claim a slip-opinion read. NO CITATOR WAS RUN - no Shepard's, no KeyCite - so subsequent history beyond the recorded Bingle affirmance is unconfirmed. The Bingle affirmance is an ORDER on the Chancery court's reasoning, not a signed opinion, and the receipt says so (BL-142). READING PASS 2026-08-10 (BL-230): the slip opinions for the four 2024-2026 decisions were READ IN FULL from the courts' own servers - Giuliano, Brewer, In re TransUnion and Marchner from the Delaware Courts opinion server, and the Brewer interlocutory disposition from the Supreme Court's own order. Case numbers, judges, dates and dispositions are taken from those documents. THE BREWER INTERLOCUTORY APPEAL NOW CORROBORATES: Turner v. Brewer, No. 444, 2025 (Del. 15 Dec. 2025), 'IT IS ORDERED that the interlocutory appeal is REFUSED' - parties reverse on appeal, and it is an ORDER not a signed opinion. Two corrections to what the receipts previously SAID about Brewer: there was no information-systems theory rejected (the opinion contains no such analysis; what was dismissed was Count II, the officers, entirely, and Count I as to directors not on the board during the wrongdoing, while the Massey claim was declined rather than rejected), and the red flag was a draft complaint sent TO THE BOARD, not something discussed in board minutes. In re TransUnion cites Sorenson six times approvingly and Bingle ONCE for black-letter - do not describe it as endorsing Bingle. Marchner gained C.A. No. 2025-0164-LWW and Will, V.C.; its slip opinion's own date line reads 'March 30, 2025' against a 'Date Submitted: December 22, 2025' in the same header, which is a typo in the court's document - the year is 2026. SUBSEQUENT-CITATION SWEEP 2026-08-10 (BL-230), AND IT IS NOT A CITATOR. No Shepard's and no KeyCite have ever been run on this block. What was run is a sweep of a FREE index (CourtListener, Del. Supr. and Del. Ch.) plus a direct read of the one later decision it surfaced. Weaker than a citator in two ways: no editorial treatment flags, and the free index is demonstrably incomplete - it holds NO reporter citation for In re TransUnion while a sitting Chancellor cites that case at 324 A.3d 869. FOUND: no appeal, reversal, vacatur or superseding decision for In re TransUnion, Giuliano, Marchner or Sorenson; the Bingle affirmance date independently confirmed at Del. Supr. No. 411, 2022, filed 17 May 2023; both Brewer WL cites and both dates confirmed by Chancellor McCormick citing her own decisions in LACERS v. Sanford (Del. Ch. 16 Jan. 2026); and In re TransUnion DISTINGUISHED in that same decision on 'effective inaction', pincited 888-90 - its holding stands but the boundary is drawn. The pre-2024 landmarks were NOT swept

sources.label: SEC cybersecurity disclosure rule
sources.intervalBecause: A disclosure clock, where the harm from a missed amendment is a LATE FILING and is asymmetric — nobody is penalised for reading the rule too often. The operative text of these instruments is comparatively stable; the staff interpretation around them is not, and it is the interpretation that moves a deadline. 365 days would let a changed clock sit unnoticed for up to a year on the one artifact whose value is being on time. Halved to 180 on 2026-08-09.

sources.version: pending; no Commission action recorded as at 2026-08-09. A petition is not a proposal and not a rule — this row exists because the product now names it, and a claim about pendency decays the moment the Commission acts
sources.intervalBecause: the claim carried in the product is that the Commission HAS NOT ACTED. That is a negative about a live docket, and the day it stops being true every sentence citing it becomes wrong. 365 days is a year of being wrong; the disclosure-clock rows moved to 180 for the weaker version of the same argument
